add.k: Hobie Brown, a petty crook in a stealth battle suit
st: In season 4, petty crook Hobie Brown becomes the Prowler in the Kingpin's suit, then teams with Spider-Man to escape its trap and quits crime.

files.notes: No transcript of the 1994 series is on springfieldspringfield (only five season 1 episodes are listed, none of these), so names and events rest on the Marvel Database episode and character pages and the Wikipedia episode list. Hobie works in Iceberg's gang, but the gang is never given a name, so Independent. The Kingpin controls him through the rigged suit, but Hobie never does a job for him, so Fisk's Empire is not used. Raft file because most of what he does is crime; he ends Allied after teaming with Spider-Man and giving up crime.

add.k: An icy crime boss who runs Hobie Brown's gang
st: In season 4, crime boss Iceberg orders Hobie Brown killed for skimming loot, until Hobie returns as the Prowler and beats him.

files.notes: No transcript of the 1994 series is on springfieldspringfield (only five season 1 episodes are listed, none of these), so names and events rest on the Marvel Database episode and character pages and the Wikipedia episode list. He appears only in Hobie's telling of his story. His gang has no name on screen, so Independent; the Marvel Database says he worked under the Kingpin, which the episode pages do not show, so Fisk's Empire is not used. What happens to him after the Prowler beats him is not shown and he is never caught, so At large (checker). op is the Prowler, the only one who fights him.

add.k: Dr. Wolfgang Groitzig's daughter, living in Moscow
st: In season 5, Illyena shows Peter and Robbie the evidence her father kept that clears Peter's parents, until the Chameleon takes it.

files.notes: No transcript of the 1994 series is on springfieldspringfield (only five season 1 episodes are listed, none of these), so names and events rest on the Marvel Database episode and character pages and the Wikipedia episode list. She is named in Six Forgotten Warriors (54) before she appears in Unclaimed Legacy (55), where she is also seen as a young girl when Richard and Mary Parker visit her father. The Chameleon steals the evidence disguised as her husband Karl. No group, so Independent.

add.k: A gang boss who drives the giant Big Wheel
st: In season 3, Jackson Weele's jet-pack gang runs a protection racket, and he chases Robert Farrell in his Big Wheel until it crashes.

files.notes: No transcript of the 1994 series is on springfieldspringfield (only five season 1 episodes are listed, none of these), so names and events rest on the Marvel Database episode and character pages and the Wikipedia episode list. The batch lists him as Big Wheel, but both sources call him Jackson Weele and use Big Wheel for his vehicle, so n is Jackson Weele. Spider-Man and Robert wreck the Big Wheel, Spider-Man webs Weele out before it sinks, and he is jailed. His gang has no name on screen, so Independent. Robert Farrell (Rocket Racer) is in another batch, so no tie to him.

add.k: A Six American Warriors hero with a thunderous voice
st: In season 5, the Thunderer, who has guarded the doomsday site as a homeless man for fifty years, fights beside Spider-Man and the Six.

files.notes: No transcript of the 1994 series is on springfieldspringfield (only five season 1 episodes are listed, none of these), so names and events rest on the Marvel Database episode and character pages and the Wikipedia episode list. His real name Jerry Carstairs could not be confirmed as said on screen, so k leaves it out. He is first seen in the World War II story in Secrets of the Six (56), then fights in The Six Fight Again (57) and The Price of Heroism (58); afterwards the five warriors go back into retirement, so Retired. Whizzer, Miss America and Omar Mosely are in another batch, so no ties to them.

add.k: An astronaut, J. Jonah Jameson's son
st: In season 1, John Jameson crash-lands with Promethium X and an alien ooze, then the Shocker holds him for ransom until Spider-Man frees him.

files.notes: No transcript of the 1994 series is on springfieldspringfield (only five season 1 episodes are listed, none of these), so names and events rest on the Marvel Database episode and character pages and the Wikipedia episode list. The Marvel Database lists him in all three Alien Costume parts, but in Part Three only his space probe is used to carry the symbiote away, so the step ends with Part Two (8). His space agency is never named on the episode pages, so Independent. He is only referred to in Guilty (42).

k: A portal scientist hired by Wilson Fisk
The Spot, a scientist covered in living portals
st: In season 3, Fisk funds Dr. Ohnn's portal work until he becomes the Spot and robs banks, then turns on the Kingpin and seals the rift.

files.notes: No transcript of the 1994 series is on springfieldspringfield (only five season 1 episodes are listed, none of these), so names and events rest on the Marvel Database episode and character pages and the Wikipedia episode list. Tony Stark fires him from Stark Enterprises at the very start of The Spot (39), his only episode; he then works in Fisk's lab, serving Fisk's Empire unknowingly and later under threat. He turns on the Kingpin at the end of 39, so the Independent stage is keyed to 39 (checker). The k stage for the Spot name is keyed to 39 as well, since the name comes partway through that episode. He jumps into the portal to close it and Silvia Lopez follows; his fate is left open, so Missing. Silvia Lopez is in another batch, so no tie to her.

add.k: An old contact of Jameson's who runs a supper club
st: In season 4, Joey Nails straps Jameson into a chair at his supper club, until Jameson turns the tables and gets the tip he needs.

files.notes: No transcript of the 1994 series is on springfieldspringfield (only five season 1 episodes are listed, none of these), so names and events rest on the Marvel Database episode and character pages and the Wikipedia episode list. The Marvel Database names his club Baby Joe's, which could not be confirmed as said or shown, so Independent. He is shady but not one of the Kingpin's people and does not work against the heroes beyond this scene, so a Compound file.

k: A S.H.I.E.L.D. commander, Ben Parker's old friend
The Destroyer, a World War II super soldier
st: In season 5, Commander Keene Marlow visits May, then becomes the Destroyer again to fight the Kingpin and the Red Skull with Spider-Man.

Secrets of the Six (56) shows him as the Destroyer in World War II, where his wife Lenora dies and he leaves his ring with Ben; he fights as the Destroyer again from The Six Fight Again (57), so the group stage is keyed there. Afterwards the five warriors go back into retirement, so Retired. Whizzer, Miss America and Omar Mosely are in another batch.

add.k: A man who finds a lost portal machine in Central Park
st: In season 3, Lenny tries to pawn a portal machine he found, sets it off by accident, and Spider-Man has to pull him clear.

st: In season 5, years earlier in Russia, Mary and Richard hand Dr. Groitzig their evidence, and Mary comforts his young daughter Illyena.
In season 3, an illusion of Mary welcomes Peter into Baron Mordo's cult, until Doctor Strange breaks the spell.

The episodes call her and Richard American spies but name no agency, so Independent. Richard Parker and Dr. Groitzig are in another batch, so no ties to them.

add.k: A scarred movie star, kept alive by Mysterio
st: In season 4, scarred actress Miranda Wilson, now a cyborg, captures Mary Jane to steal her body, then frees her and dies with Quentin Beck.

files.notes: No transcript of the 1994 series is on springfieldspringfield (only five season 1 episodes are listed, none of these), so names and events rest on the Marvel Database episode and character pages and the Wikipedia episode list. Her accident on the Brooklyn Bridge is shown in a past scene in the same episode. The movie she starred in is never tied to a named company on the episode pages, and Wonder Studios is only where it is shot, so Independent. The wiki marks her death as apparent; she is left in the exploding complex, so Deceased.

add.k: A lizard made smart and strong by Connors' DNA
st: In season 4, Monitor, a reptile changed by Connors' DNA, kidnaps Connors with Gila and Gecko, until he is turned back into a lizard.

files.notes: No transcript of the 1994 series is on springfieldspringfield (only five season 1 episodes are listed, none of these), so names and events rest on the Marvel Database episode and character pages and the Wikipedia episode list. The lizard trio has no group name, so Independent. Gila and Gecko are in another batch, so no ties to them. At the end he is turned back into an ordinary reptile and is not caught, so At large (checker).

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Spider-Man stops Hobie Brown from stealing Mary Jane's purse and sends him back to jail. As the Prowler, Hobie later beats Spider-Man, then tells Peter everything and teams with Spider-Man to break into the Kingpin's base and free himself from the suit.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who jails him and then frees him
stages.whoB: The Prowler, a crook who beats him and then needs him

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Hobie runs petty robberies for the crime boss Iceberg and skims some of the loot. Iceberg has his men try to kill him, and Hobie later returns as the Prowler and defeats him.
stages.whoA: Iceberg, the crime boss who wants him dead
stages.whoB: Hobie Brown, the crook who skims his loot

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: In prison Hobie saves Richard Fisk, so the Kingpin gets him released and gives him a stealth battle suit. The suit then shocks him and the Kingpin says he controls him, until Hobie and Spider-Man find a way to disarm it.
stages.whoA: The Kingpin, who traps him in a rigged suit
stages.whoB: The Prowler, a crook he tries to control

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Hobie saves Richard Fisk from another prisoner's attack in prison. Richard tells his father, who repays Hobie by clearing his name.
stages.whoA: Richard Fisk, whose life he saves in prison
stages.whoB: Hobie Brown, who saves his life in prison

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Peter and Robbie track Illyena down in Moscow. She tells Peter his parents were not traitors and shows them the details her father hid, before the Chameleon steals them.
stages.whoA: Peter Parker, Richard and Mary's son
stages.whoB: Illyena Groitzig, who clears his parents

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Robbie gets Illyena's address from his friend Boris Pushkin and brings Peter to her. She shows them the evidence her father kept on the Doomsday device.
stages.whoA: Robbie Robertson, a Daily Bugle editor
stages.whoB: Illyena Groitzig, Groitzig's daughter

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: The Chameleon poses as Illyena's husband Karl. He takes the evidence she shows Peter and Robbie and leads Spider-Man into a trap.
stages.whoA: The Chameleon, posing as her husband
stages.whoB: Illyena Groitzig, whose husband he poses as

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Spider-Man fights Jackson Weele's jet-pack gang and saves Robert Farrell from the Big Wheel. He and Robert wreck its timing, and Spider-Man webs Weele out before it plunges into the water.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who wrecks his Big Wheel
stages.whoB: Jackson Weele, a gang boss on the Big Wheel

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: The Thunderer fights beside Captain America in the Six American Warriors during World War II. When Cap returns from the vortex fifty years later, they fight the Red Skull together again, and Cap is trapped once more.
stages.whoA: Captain America, his old team leader
stages.whoB: The Thunderer, one of the Six

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: The Thunderer and Keene Marlow, the Destroyer, serve together in the Six American Warriors. Fifty years later they reunite to fight the Kingpin's Insidious Six and the Red Skull.
stages.whoA: The Destroyer, his old teammate
stages.whoB: The Thunderer, his old teammate

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Spider-Man fights beside the Thunderer and the other warriors against the Insidious Six. Together they take on the Red Skull and Electro.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who fights beside the Six
stages.whoB: The Thunderer, one of the Six

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: The Thunderer and the Six try to stop the Red Skull's doomsday plot in World War II. When the Skull is freed fifty years later, the Thunderer fights him again.
stages.whoA: The Red Skull, the Six's old enemy
stages.whoB: The Thunderer, one of the Six

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: The Red Skull's doomsday device turns his son Kragov into Electro. The Thunderer and the Six fight him with Spider-Man.
stages.whoA: Electro, the Red Skull's son
stages.whoB: The Thunderer, one of the Six

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: John is J. Jonah Jameson's son, and his crash leads Jonah to put a bounty on Spider-Man. When Jonah visits him in hospital, John tells him the Rhino was at the scene, and Jonah calls the bounty off.
stages.whoA: His father, J. Jonah Jameson
stages.whoB: His son John, an astronaut

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Spider-Man saves John and his copilot from the crashed shuttle on the bridge. When the Shocker kidnaps John for ransom, Spider-Man brings him back.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who saves him twice
stages.whoB: John Jameson, the astronaut he saves

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Alistair Smythe sends the Shocker to kidnap John from his hospital bed. The Shocker holds him for ransom for the Promethium X until Spider-Man frees him.
stages.whoA: The Shocker, who kidnaps him
stages.whoB: John Jameson, his ransom hostage

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: After John's shuttle crashes on the George Washington Bridge, the Kingpin sends the Rhino to steal the Promethium X. John later tells his father the Rhino was there.
stages.whoA: The Rhino, who robs his shuttle
stages.whoB: John Jameson, the astronaut whose shuttle he robs

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Wilson Fisk gives Dr. Ohnn a lab to continue his portal research, and Ohnn hides his new powers from him. The Kingpin takes Silvia hostage to force the Spot to capture Spider-Man, but Ohnn double-crosses him, and Fisk then lends him a plane to close the rift.
stages.whoA: Wilson Fisk, who funds and then threatens him
stages.whoB: Dr. Ohnn, the scientist he funds

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Spider-Man chases the Spot through two robberies and loses him through his portals. Forced by the Kingpin to bring in Spider-Man, Ohnn instead tells him the truth, and they fake his capture to save Silvia.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who fights and then helps him
stages.whoB: The Spot, a portal thief

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Tony Stark shuts down Dr. Ohnn's portal project after the trouble with Carnage and Dormammu and fires him. Ohnn is bitter and takes Fisk's offer.
stages.whoA: Tony Stark, who fires him
stages.whoB: Dr. Ohnn, the scientist he fires

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Jameson goes back to his old contact Joey Nails for information to clear Robbie. Joey has him restrained in a chair, but Jameson gets free, locks Joey in it instead and takes what he needs.
stages.whoA: Jigsaw Jameson, an old contact who outwits him
stages.whoB: Joey Nails, a shady old contact

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Keene Marlow, an old friend of Ben's, visits May at the Parker home. Peter overhears them talking about what May must tell him about his parents.
stages.whoA: May Parker, his late friend Ben's wife
stages.whoB: Keene Marlow, Ben's old friend

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Keene and Ben grow up as friends who dream of being heroes. After Keene's wife Lenora dies, he gives Ben his costume and ring to keep.
stages.whoA: Ben Parker, his childhood friend
stages.whoB: Keene Marlow, his childhood friend

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Keene visits May and meets her nephew Peter. As the Destroyer, he fights beside Spider-Man against the Insidious Six and the Red Skull.
stages.whoA: Peter Parker, Ben's nephew
stages.whoB: Keene Marlow, Uncle Ben's old friend

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Keene Marlow serves S.H.I.E.L.D. as a commander under Nick Fury. Both are drawn into the hunt for the doomsday weapon.
stages.whoA: Nick Fury, his S.H.I.E.L.D. chief
stages.whoB: Commander Keene Marlow, a S.H.I.E.L.D. officer

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Keene fights beside Captain America as the Destroyer in the Six American Warriors during World War II. When Cap returns from the vortex, they fight the Red Skull together again.
stages.whoA: Captain America, his old team leader
stages.whoB: The Destroyer, one of the Six

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: The Destroyer and the Six try to stop the Red Skull's doomsday plot in World War II. When the Skull is freed fifty years later, the Destroyer fights him again.
stages.whoA: The Red Skull, the Six's old enemy
stages.whoB: The Destroyer, one of the Six

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Lenny sets off the time dilation accelerator in a pawn shop and it starts pulling everything in, him included. Spider-Man arrives to save the people there before the Hobgoblin ambushes him.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who saves him
stages.whoB: Lenny, a man caught in his own portal

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Baron Mordo shows Peter an illusion of his parents, and Mary speaks to him until Doctor Strange frees him. Later Illyena reveals that Mary and Richard were not traitors but American spies who tried to stop the Doomsday device.
stages.whoA: Peter Parker, her son
stages.whoB: Mary Parker, his late mother

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Mary and Richard come to warn Illyena's father that they have been found out. Mary comforts the young Illyena, who has been listening, and is reminded of her own son.
stages.whoA: Illyena, Groitzig's young daughter
stages.whoB: Mary Parker, the spy who comforts her

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Quentin Beck finds the scarred Miranda under Wonder Studios and keeps her alive as a cyborg. He admits the body swap could never work and that he loves her as she is, and he stays with her as the complex explodes.
stages.whoA: Quentin Beck, who loves her
stages.whoB: Miranda Wilson, the star he loves

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Mary Jane gets Miranda's old leading role, and Miranda captures her to swap their bodies. When the swap fails, Miranda lets her go.
stages.whoA: Mary Jane, the look-alike she captures
stages.whoB: Miranda Wilson, who tries to steal her body

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Spider-Man comes into the tunnels under Wonder Studios to rescue Mary Jane from Miranda's machine. He gets Mary Jane out as the complex explodes.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who saves Mary Jane from her
stages.whoB: Miranda Wilson, a cyborg who captures Mary Jane

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Monitor and the other lizards kidnap Curt Connors, calling him their father. Connors becomes the Lizard and leads them, until Margaret, Debra and Mary Jane change him and the lizards back.
stages.whoA: Curt Connors, the 'father' he kidnaps
stages.whoB: Monitor, a lizard made from his DNA

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Spider-Man follows Monitor and the lizards into the sewers to rescue Connors and Mary Jane. The lizards lock him up with Gila when she is called a traitor.
stages.whoA: Spider-Man, who chases him into the sewers
stages.whoB: Monitor, one of the lizard trio

stages.title: Spider-Man (1994)
stages.text: Monitor and the lizards kidnap Mary Jane along with Connors. She escapes and helps change Connors and the lizards back.
stages.whoA: Mary Jane, who he kidnaps
stages.whoB: Monitor, a lizard who kidnaps her

dropped.why: The episode synopses for The Mutant Agenda and Mutants' Revenge show him leading the team that takes Beast and talking to the Kingpin, but no summary shows anyone saying or showing the name Lewald on screen (the character page notes it is a nod to story editor Eric Lewald), and no transcript exists, so the name test is not met.

The Make a Wish synopsis has Anastasia Hardy host his demonstration and Doctor Octopus confront him, but it does not show his name said or shown on screen, and no transcript exists, so the name test is not met.

changes.why: The episode synopses for The Mutant Agenda and Mutants' Revenge show him leading the team that takes Beast and talking to the Kingpin, but no summary shows anyone saying or showing the name Lewald on screen (the character page notes it is a nod to story editor Eric Lewald), and no transcript exists, so the name test is not met.

The Make a Wish synopsis has Anastasia Hardy host his demonstration and Doctor Octopus confront him, but it does not show his name said or shown on screen, and no transcript exists, so the name test is not met.

He turns on the Kingpin in The Spot (39), his only episode, so the change to Independent belongs at #39, not #40 where he is only mentioned. The same synopsis opens with Tony Stark firing him from the Stark Enterprises portal project, so he is shown serving Stark Enterprises first.
The Prowler beats him, and neither the Marvel Database synopsis nor the Wikipedia summary shows him caught, killed or vanished: a crime boss left free is At large, not Missing.
Mary Jane, Margaret and Debra return him to an ordinary reptile; no summary shows him captured, killed or lost, so At large fits better than Missing.
